name: LangGraph
one_liner: Low-level orchestration for long-running, stateful agents.
what_it_is: A low-level orchestration framework for building, managing and deploying long-running, stateful agents, in its own words, taking inspiration from Pregel and Apache Beam. Control flow is expressed as an explicit graph of steps with state carried between them.
why_it_matters: Making the graph explicit is what lets an agent be paused, resumed, inspected and retried at a step boundary — the difference between a demo and something you can operate. The cost is that a task genuinely served by one call now carries a graph, a state schema and a persistence decision.
suitable_for: Agents that run long enough to need resuming
Flows requiring human approval partway through
Work where you must inspect why an agent took a branch
not_suitable_for: Single-turn calls, where the graph is ceremony around one request
Teams unwilling to own state persistence
Prototypes where the flow is still changing every hour
